messages:
alex: Ran a perf sweep on the prod-like rig this morning. Seeing a pretty lopsided prefill vs decode split and some tail spikes at p99. dropping raw profiler snippet below

maya: paste the numbers? quick summary pls

alex: sure — high level: prefill is decent but decode dominates tail. KV hit rate is middling which seems to amplify decode cost on cold/miss. sample: 
```
model: redwood-4x
seq_len: 512
microbatch: 8 (adaptive)
kernel-path: tiled->matmul-v2->matmul-v1 fallback
prefill: p50 22ms p95 62ms p99 160ms
decode:  p50 48ms p95 220ms p99 540ms
throughput: 120 rps
KV hit rate: 0.62 overall, 0.38 for long sessions
notes: decode p99 correlates with KV misses and kernel fallback to matmul-v1
```

sofia: 0.62 is low for steady state. cold sessions + fallback explains 540ms p99. did you capture per-kernel timings (tiled vs matmul)?

alex: per-kernel breakdown: tiled avg decode 30ms, matmul-v2 65ms, matmul-v1 210ms. fallback occurrences spike when sequence > 400 and batch composition includes long contexts. kernel selector currently picks based on sequence median and estimated batch occupancy.

liam: that suggests selector thresholds are too aggressive toward matmul-v1 for mixed-length microbatches. two levers: 1) tighten threshold so tiled stays for decode up to 512 when batch fraction short, 2) bias decode to prefer tiled if KV hit rate > X.

maya: microbatch sizing tradeoff? what if we increase microbatch to 16?

alex: tested that briefly: 
```
microbatch=8 -> throughput 120 rps, p99 decode 540ms
microbatch=16 -> throughput 180 rps, p99 decode 720ms (more fallback + queueing)
```
so microbatch=16 helped throughput but worsened tail. p95 moved a bit but p99 degraded due to longer coalesced batches exposing more long-seq requests and increasing fallback probability.

sofia: agreed — tail matters for SLO. We should optimize for p99 while keeping throughput target. Proposed approach: 
- small kernel-selector change: prefer tiled for decode unless >70% of microbatch has seq>512
- KV prefetch policy: when session has seen >1 request in last 30s, prefetch next N tokens' KV into fast cache
- adaptive microbatching: cap max microbatch for decode path at 12 for latency-tier customers

liam: +1. Also we can add a lightweight per-request heuristic: if KV hit rate < 0.5 and request seq>256, force single-request execution (no coalescing) to avoid polluting microbatch and causing fallback churn.

maya: can we run an A/B with: control=current selector + microbatch 8 vs experiment=selector tweak + prefetch + microbatch cap 12? metric targets: p99 <= 500ms and throughput >=110 rps.

alex: yes. I can spin up canary with the selector tweak and prefetch turned on for 5% traffic. Will attach profiler traces.

zane-bot: deploy-bot: canary job created (#3458) for kernel-selector-v0.3 with warm-kv-prefetch. ETA: 30m queue.

liam: also add perf counters for per-kernel invocation rate and KV-prefetch hit ratio so we can attribute wins. simple prometheus labels: kernel="tiled"/"matmul-v2"/"matmul-v1", path="prefill"/"decode"

sofia: action items: 
- alex: run 5% canary, collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel usage + kv-prefetch hit, due EOD
- liam: instrument counters and add dashboard tiles (kernel share, kv hit by session length), due tomorrow AM
- maya: prepare customer SLO impact note and rollback plan if p99 worsens for latency tier customers, due EOD

alex: noted. I'll include a short trace snippet in #perf-results and flag any regressions. thanks. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks team. if canary is green we'll promote and then iterate on microbatch cap tuning.

alex: one more datapoint — if we enable kv warmup for 80% of returning sessions p99 drops ~120ms in my synthetic replay. promising but need real traffic test.

sofia: ok lets run it. keep messages short in the canary thread so we can correlate with alerts.

zane-bot: incident-bot: alert rule p99_decode > 500ms triggered for canary (minute 12) - investigating

alex: saw the alert, rolling back prefetch on canary while we inspect logs. will report findings in next 30m.
